verificationMethod: Live network capture of a real headless-Chromium Playwright session against https://saudi.hardees.me/en/home (research/pickup/raw/, research/delivery/raw/ - git-ignored raw HARs + api-calls.json; sanitized copies retained under research/pickup/sanitized/, research/delivery/sanitized/).

Two full end-to-end runs of tools/capture-network.js (--channel=pickup and --channel=delivery), plus five earlier exploratory Playwright sessions during development of that tool - see investigation-log.md for the full session-by-session trail.

Direct same-origin fetch() calls executed from inside the already-authenticated browser tab (page.evaluate) to sample all 12 real menu categories and to probe several frontend-discovered endpoints (getNutritionInfo, getPrepTime, product, product-bundle-step, getPromotion) without fighting the product grid's lazy-rendered click targets.

Static analysis of the site's own production JS bundles (spwa-ui-e89ec732.js, index-41f2264d.js) - the literal endpoint-definition table and request-thunk implementations - as a first pass for endpoints that were hard to trigger live, then labeled per-endpoint below by exactly how far live verification actually got (see research/shared/frontend-analysis/bundle-findings.md for the full table and labeling convention).

A small, sequential, low-volume direct-HTTP (no browser) probe using Node's built-in https module, formalized as tools/probe-public-api.js - see research/shared/sample-requests/direct-http-probe-transcript.md.
notes: This file documents PUBLIC, unauthenticated (guest-session) endpoints only. No login, OTP, payment, cart, or checkout endpoint was ever called by this investigation.

Hardee's Saudi runs on the SAME 'AMR' (Americana Restaurants) backend platform family as KFC Saudi (competitors/kfc/) - getAppConfig's response carries an 'amr':{...} block, and Hardee's own guest-session localStorage.profileDraft carries 'appbundle':'com.kfc.me' (a shared mobile-app bundle id across the group's brand apps). This explains why several endpoint NAMES resemble KFC's (getMenuConfig, getMenu, getProductsByCategory, getNewStore, validateLocation, getStoreList, guestLogin, getAppConfig, getHome, getProgressivePromotion). It does NOT mean the payloads/response shapes are identical - every endpoint below was independently re-verified against Hardee's own live responses; see each endpoint's verificationNote for the concrete differences found (e.g. getStoreList's much richer store object, getProductsByCategory's nested items[]/steps[] product structure, the 'delevery' misspelling, the day-of-week displayDay offer field).

'Session' fields (cookies, deviceid, the 't'/'_t'/'lat'/'lrt' JWT cookies) are captured fresh per run by tools/capture-network.js and held only in the Playwright browser context's own cookie jar for that process. They are NEVER written into this file, api-map.md, git, or any log - see 'Security & sensitive data notes' in api-map.md.

The site's edge sits behind an Azure Application Gateway WAF that returns a plain HTML 403 for any request missing browser-shaped user-agent/origin/referer headers - live-confirmed directly (see tools/probe-public-api.js output). This is the same WAF behavior documented for saudi.kfc.me, independently re-confirmed here on saudi.hardees.me's own domain.

Sentinel values confirmed live and independently re-verified from KFC's documented pattern: specialPrice<=0 (observed exactly 0) does NOT mean free - it means 'this bundle_group wrapper does not carry a simple fixed-discount price here', while its own promoId is still a real positive value. promoId=-1 means 'no active offer'. See the quirks list in api-map.md.

UPDATED 2026-08-06 (second research session): /api/product and /api/product-bundle-step are now FULLY RESOLVED and live-verified with populated data (see their endpoint entries below and unresolved-items.md item #1's resolution) - the missing fields in the first session's guesses were `categoryId` and `service`. `getPromotion` remains unresolved (still 500/DEFAULT_VALIDATION_ERROR on every payload guessed - it was not part of this session's resolution work). getMenuConfig's 'channel-independent for one cluster' finding was RE-TESTED this session against a second branch ~950km away (Jeddah, storeId=97/7) with identical results - see api-map.md 'Channel separation mechanism' update and unresolved-items.md item #9.

UPDATED 2026-08-11 (fourth session): a real, working production Node.js collector (competitors/hardees/collector/) and Python backend/dashboard were built and live-verified end to end (both channels, 12/12 categories, 110 real products each, status SUCCESS) - see ../../README.md and the note at the top of api-map.md. Confirmed the production branch is EUROMARCHE-H (storeId=24) via a full getStoreList dump of 46 real Riyadh branches, matching the storeId=24 used as an example throughout this file's earlier sessions. Three real, previously-undiscovered issues were found and fixed while building the collector (none were caught by the earlier research-only sessions, which never exercised a full run): (1) getStoreList's response carries a leading UTF-8 BOM that breaks JSON.parse(); (2) saudi.hardees.me's own TLS certificate was found expired at verification time; (3) getStoreList intermittently returns a transient Azure BlobNotFound 500 that clears within 1-2s on retry.

endpoints.verificationNote: MAJOR FINDING - see api-map.md 'Channel separation'. Every single getMenuConfig call observed live in this investigation ({"orderType":"PICKUP"}, {"orderType":"DELIVERY"}, {"orderType":"PICKUP","storeId":24}, {"orderType":"PICKUP","storeId":5796}) returned the IDENTICAL {"menuConfigId":"HRD_SA_23","clusterId":"1_8"} - across both the Pickup and Delivery capture-network.js runs, and across multiple manual exploration sessions on 2026-08-06. This is the opposite of what was assumed going in (that this would be the channel-fixing call, as it is for KFC) - for THIS branch/cluster, orderType and storeId did not change the resolved config at all. RE-CONFIRMED in a second research session against a Jeddah branch (storeId=97 Pickup, storeId=7 Delivery, ~950km from the original Riyadh branch, cityId=31 vs 11) via TWO fully separate Playwright browser contexts (separate guest sessions/deviceids/cookies) - every getMenuConfig call in BOTH sessions again resolved the identical HRD_SA_23/1_8, with the identical 12-category list and byte-identical prices on every one of 40+ products spot-checked (see research/shared/sample-responses/channel-comparison-jeddah-vs-riyadh.json). This strongly suggests Hardee's Saudi uses ONE NATIONWIDE cluster for this channel-independence behavior, not a per-branch quirk - though see unresolved-items.md item #9 for what is still not proven (a delivery-fee/minimum-order cart-level difference remains untested).

endpoints.verificationNote: RESOLUTION: discovered by driving a REAL 'Customize' click in a real Playwright browser (the button is a styled <span>, not a <button> element, and product cards measure 0x0 until their lazy-load image observer fires at least once - see investigation-log.md) and inspecting the exact request it sent: {id,cluster,service,categoryId,Language,menuConfigId}. Live-confirmed for: burger/simple (id=9074 'Super Star Mushroom Sandwich' -> 15 condiment options with Regular/Extra sub-tiers); meal/box (wrapper id=77772960 'Roast Beef Box' -> its items[] entry with id=12187 'Roast Beef Box - Regular' returns 7 fully-populated steps: Choice of Box/Sandwich/condiments(12)/side(6)/Beverages(6)/Tender(2)/AddOns(11); switching the SIZE variant to 'Large' inside the modal re-issued this same call with id=12189, a DIFFERENT nested item, price 44 vs Regular's 39); side/configurable (id=9118 'Crispy Curls' -> SIZE variant Medium/Large, also fired /api/productUpgrades with a near-identical payload {productId,menuConfigId}); drink-dessert/configurable (id=9121 'Mini Churros' -> FLAVOR variant Sweet Creamy/Caramel); promotional item (wrapper id=77772554 'Double Treat Meal', originalPrice=65/specialPrice=49/promoId=6544 -> its items[] entry with id=10545 -> 14 steps: two independent sandwich/condiment/side/beverage step-pairs plus one shared Add Ons step; the nested item's OWN originalPrice=49 already equals the wrapper's specialPrice, i.e. the discount is 'baked into' the nested item rather than double-applied). Also re-verified against a second, ~950km-distant branch (Jeddah, storeId=97/7) with byte-identical results - see api-map.md 'Channel separation mechanism' update. CORRECTION (2026-08-06, Streamlit-integration session): the nested-item-id lookup rule stated above and in earlier passes of this file was imprecise - the wrapper's `selectedItem` field is that item's **sku**, not its **id** (live-confirmed: wrapper 77772960's selectedItem=945, a sku, matching items[] entry id=12187 - sending 945 itself also returns an empty data:{}). Correct rule: match `items[].sku == wrapper.selectedItem`, then use that entry's `id`. Caught by a live smoke test while building services/menu_service.py::resolve_detail_lookup_id() for the Streamlit preview page - every concrete id value quoted above (12187, 12189, 10545) was and remains correct; only the one-line derivation rule was wrong.
